draft.title: Terminating and recurring decimals
card: To turn a fraction into a decimal, divide the top number by the bottom number. For 3/8, divide 3 by 8 to get 0.375.
a decimal that ends, such as 3/8 = 0.375 or 1/4 = 0.25.
a decimal whose digits repeat forever, such as 1/3 = 0.333... A dot or bar over the repeating digits shows this, so 2/3 = 0.6 with a bar over the 6.
Worked example: 5/6 = 5 ÷ 6 = 0.8333..., where only the 3 repeats. The 8 is not part of the repeat.
draft.remember: Divide top by bottom. The decimal either ends or repeats.

a.q: Which fraction is a recurring decimal?
a.why: 2 ÷ 9 = 0.222..., and the 2 repeats forever. The others end: 3/5 = 0.6, 7/8 = 0.875 and 1/2 = 0.5.
a.clue: Divide each top number by its bottom number and see which never stops.

b.q: Sam divides 1 by 6 on a calculator and gets 0.16666... How should he show this recurring decimal?
opts: 0.1666 and stop, because it is a terminating decimal
b.why: Only the 6 repeats, so the dot or bar goes over the 6 alone and the 1 stays outside it. Repeating both digits would mean 0.161616..., which is a different number.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: 2/9 = 0.222... recurs, and 1/6 = 0.1666... with only the 6 repeating.
